rationale:
The example `requirements.sdk.graph.hierarchical-paths` gives a concrete case. It defines a `HabeasNodeId::Requirement(Vec<String>)` enum, and a `node_path` mapping for it turns `a.b.c` into `["requirement","a","b","c"]`. The expected behavior is that mapping.

The test is `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/contracts.rs#fn[hierarchical_requirement_identity_maps_each_component_to_a_path_segment]`, and it carries a `{test}` reference to the example. It:
- Declares the same enum shape, with only the `Requirement` variant.
- Defines `node_path` as a closure that prepends "requirement" to the components.
- Builds `Requirement(["a","b","c"])`.
- Asserts that the path segments equal `["requirement","a","b","c"]`. This is the example's stated outcome.
- Asserts that converting the same id twice gives equal `NodePath`s. This is the determinism part of the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.node_path_method`.

The example is illustrative. It prescribes no concrete SDK code beyond the user-defined mapping, so a local enum and closure are an appropriate way to exercise it. The cited `node_path_method` requirement is context only. The test asserts every outcome the example states, so I found no gap.
